limits: Design guidance from case studies, no measurements
Type 2 growth concern for million-row dimensions deferred to Chapter 6
Rapidly changing dimensions and surrogate key workflow deferred to Chapters 6 and 16
Written in 2002; no mention of modern warehouse features such as MERGE or columnar engines
practices: Choose blended vs separate transaction fact tables by user analytic needs, number of distinct business processes, number of source systems and dimensionality of facts (pp.91-92).
Make control numbers such as PO and check numbers degenerate dimensions (p.91).
Ask business representatives about change tracking up front; do not assume they do not care (p.95).
Use type 1 overwrite for corrections or when old values have no value; it keeps no history and requires rebuilding aggregates (p.96-97).
Use type 2 (new row, new surrogate key) as the workhorse for historically accurate attributes; never use the natural key plus version digits or effective date as the key (p.97-99).
Count products on the natural key, not the surrogate key, when type 2 rows exist (p.98).
Do not constrain on dimension effective dates to partition fact history; they are useful only for slicing the dimension itself (p.98-99).
Detect changed rows in staging with a per-row CRC checksum (p.100).
Use type 3 (added prior column) only when two views of the world are needed at once; rarely used and not 'better' than 1 or 2 (p.101-102).
Use predictable-change multiple version overlays (one column per year plus Current) for annual realignments (p.102-103).
Use the type 6 hybrid (historical plus current attribute) only if the business agrees the complexity is needed (p.104-105).
Split rapidly changing attributes into a separate dimension with its own foreign key in the fact table (p.105).
